u2fd: Always enable user keys This change deprecates the "legacy" code path, and enables legacy fallback if users have not swiched explicitly to the new code path. This is a forced migration to the new code path, while still supporting legacy key handles for authentication. For a user who has previously enabled U2F with 'u2f' or 'g2f' mode (but not switched to user keys), this change will cause new registrations to be user-specific, but old keys can still be used to authenticate. No user action is required for this behavior. BUG=b:133275654 TEST=flash u2fd prior to this change set flags to --u2f (without --user_keys) generate legacy key handle flash u2fd with this change check legacy kh still works check new kh is user-specific set flags to --u2f --user_keys check legacy kh does not work Change-Id: I3d273e5233427d8641532e3dec9664107a32672d Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1750611 Tested-by: Louis Collard <louiscollard@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Louis Collard <louiscollard@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Andrey Pronin <apronin@chromium.org>

common-mk: .gn: respect shebangs of scripts we run gn's default behavior for scripts to always use `python`. It doesn't matter if the target script has its own shebang or is a different language, gn will always run it through `python`. This causes us problems as we migrate things to Python 3 -- we set the shebang to run `python2` or `python3` explicitly, but gn still uses `python`. Lets use /usr/bin/env as a simple exec redirect. This will end up running all the scripts directly and letting the kernel parse the shebang of the script. BUG=chromium:989152 TEST=CQ passes Change-Id: I13e3b3c6ba6f37a2f975c3eac1fe510d15af1117 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1737198 Tested-by: Mike Frysinger <vapier@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Mike Frysinger <vapier@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Keigo Oka <oka@chromium.org>
